crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Brain Computer Interfaces
children.blurb: Brain computer interfaces are systems that read neural signals and translate them into commands for external devices, or write signals into the brain.

children.name: Early Signals of Dementia
children.blurb: Early signals of dementia refers to computational detection of subtle cognitive, behavioral, motor, or biomarker changes that may precede a clinical diagnosis.

children.name: Functional MRI Interpretation
children.blurb: Functional MRI interpretation uses AI to map brain activity from blood-oxygen-level-dependent signals, identify activation patterns tied to tasks or resting states, and support localization of language, motor, and memory functions before surgery.

children.name: Seizure Prediction
children.blurb: Seizure prediction is the use of machine learning to estimate the likelihood that a person with epilepsy will have a seizure within a short upcoming window, usually minutes to hours, based on physiological signals.

children.name: Cognitive Rehabilitation
children.blurb: Cognitive rehabilitation in this context covers AI systems that assess, train, and support recovery of cognitive functions such as attention, memory, executive function, and language after stroke, traumatic brain injury, or in neurodegenerative conditions.

sections.body: Neuroinformatics and the brain applies machine learning to data from the nervous system, including electrical signals, brain scans, and behavioral tests. In practice, AI models are being used to decode intended hand or cursor movements from implanted electrode arrays for people with paralysis, to flag subtle changes in speech or walking patterns that may appear years before a dementia diagnosis, and to read functional MRI scans for signs of altered brain activity. These are not hypothetical systems, they are trained on recorded neural activity, clinical notes, imaging sequences, and longitudinal patient records. The work sits inside the larger AI Physician section because each application turns a stream of biological data into a prediction or a control signal for a clinician or a device.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field has real but narrow successes. Seizure prediction models can sometimes warn of an impending event minutes in advance using scalp or implanted EEG, but false alarms remain common enough that many people cannot rely on them for daily decisions. Brain computer interfaces have let a small number of trial participants move a cursor or a robotic arm, yet the hardware is invasive, the signal drifts day to day, and the systems are not widely available outside research. Dementia signal tools can rank risk from voice or gait data, but they are not stand alone diagnostics and can be thrown off by medication, mood, or recording conditions. Functional MRI interpretation models can label regions or detect anomalies in research datasets, but they often fail when tested on a different scanner or a different hospital. Cognitive rehabilitation software can adapt exercises to a person's performance, but evidence that it slows decline is mixed and it does not replace human therapy.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for how thoughts become commands should start with Brain Computer Interfaces, which covers the hardware, decoding models, and the gap between lab demos and daily use. Early Signals of Dementia explains the passive monitoring and screening tools that look for changes in language, movement, or sleep before a formal diagnosis. Functional MRI Interpretation is the page for imaging based models that map brain activity and try to spot patterns linked to disease or injury. Seizure Prediction focuses on EEG based forecasting and the practical problem of false alarms. Cognitive Rehabilitation rounds out the section by covering software that adjusts memory, attention, or language exercises over time, and it connects back to the same underlying data and model limits described in the other pages.
